title: Consultation — Sarah Jenkins
raw_transcript:
Doctor: Good morning Sarah, please have a seat. What brings you in today?
Patient: Thank you doctor. For the past 4 days I've been having these severe throbbing headaches on both sides of my temples. They get worse when looking at computer screens at work.
Doctor: I see. Have you noticed any sensitivity to light, nausea, or visual changes like flashing lights?
Patient: No flashing lights, but bright fluorescent lights make my head pound more. No fever or stiff neck.
Doctor: Let's check your vitals. Blood pressure is 124 over 82, pulse is 74 regular, temperature 36.8 Celsius, oxygen saturation is 99%.
Doctor: Neurological examination is completely normal. Cranial nerves intact. It looks like an acute tension headache with mild cervical strain from desk posture.
Doctor: I will recommend Ibuprofen 400mg three times daily after meals for 3 days, plenty of hydration, and taking screen breaks every 45 minutes. If it persists past a week or you develop severe vomiting, please come back immediately.

soap_note.subjective: Patient reports tension headache exacerbated by screen exposure. Denies photophobia, aura, or visual disturbance.
soap_note.objective: Vitals stable. Alert and oriented x3. Pertinent physical examination findings documented per consultation dialogue.
soap_note.assessment: Tension-type headache with cervical musculoskeletal strain.
soap_note.plan:
1. Initiate recommended pharmacotherapy and supportive care.
2. Hydration and lifestyle modification as discussed.
3. Follow up in 7 days or sooner if warning signs emerge.

ai_suggestions.content: Consider first-line analgesia with gastroprotection if needed
Schedule review consultation in 7 days to evaluate treatment efficacy
Monitor for any sudden increase in symptom severity

action_items.text: Send post-consultation care plan via WhatsApp
Review lab investigations / referral if symptoms persist
